title: Keep network credentials out of settings patches
summary: Reject network authentication-token keys at ordinary WebView and Local API settings-patch boundaries while retaining an explicit backend-only credential path for network enrollment and rotation.
reason: Remediate CSW-2026-07-09-SETTINGS-001. Ordinary settings preview/save requests could carry real CoordinatorAuthToken or WorkerAuthToken values through browser memory, request bodies, and settings-patch evidence.
behavior_before: Settings preview/save rejected only the literal redaction placeholder, so real coordinator and worker authentication tokens could be submitted through the general-purpose WebView settings patch route.
behavior_after: Ordinary settings preview/save rejects coordinator and worker token keys without echoing their values, WebView commands stop them before API dispatch, and backend-owned network workflows use a non-route internal credential capability.
tests_added: Facade preview rejects both network token keys, placeholders, removals, and request-body capability-bypass attempts without returning submitted values.
Facade save rejects coordinator and worker token values without a config write while preserving an existing token during unrelated settings saves.
Live Local API preview/save requests reject both token keys without response leakage or persistence.
Backend worker join/import still persists WorkerAuthToken through the private credential path and omits it from command evidence.
WebView preview/save commands reject case-insensitive token keys before apiPost and omit submitted values from rendered command evidence.
Ordinary running-worker settings saves continue to hot-apply URL and path-map changes without accepting token mutation.
manual_validation: Modified and adjacent facade/network/WebView suites passed: 98 tests using bundled Python; touched Python Ruff checks passed.
Validation Ladder Rung 3 settings-policy and config-save-runner suites passed: 28 tests.
Settings Patch Evidence, real-browser Settings Field Matrix, and real-browser LibraryProfiles Save smoke wrappers passed against disposable config/state; no real media was used.
Direct Node WebView command-boundary proof passed: credential-bearing preview/save attempts made zero apiPost calls and emitted no secret values.

Focused Python typing passed for the network and orchestration mixins after adding type-only private-capability declarations. The candidate mixin remains outside the enforced typing boundary and retains pre-existing dynamic-key/mixin typing debt.

Targeted runtime/source summary refresh wrote ten summaries; the final packet/index refresh produced 2,524 typed project records; generated project/feature and WebView public-contract/command/touchpoint checks passed.
Architecture and risky-file checks passed. Active-doc validation retained unrelated DOC005, and dependency validation retained unrelated AUDIT-FIND-DEP-001.

Full Windows release build with -Verify -IncludeTests ran for 908.3 seconds. Package-local tool integration and end-to-end smoke passed; the wrapper exited 1 only on established generated/status-doc, dependency-cycle, unrelated Ruff, and WebView static-asset baselines.

The preserved failed candidate package contained every changed runtime/test file and passed all 98 modified and adjacent tests using its bundled Python runtime, proving packaged coordinator/worker credential behavior and WebView pre-dispatch blocking.
Both exact disposable release-validation directories were removed after packaged proof; no validation package remains.
Strict worktree coverage passed with all active change packets valid.
rollback_plan: Revert the settings-patch boundary, network internal-call migration, WebView guard, tests, generated summaries, and packet metadata together. Do not restore browser/API token submission without an independently designed native or backend credential-rotation contract.
notes: This is a high-risk settings/network credential boundary change. Existing source, scratch, output, media policy, and real media are not touched; representative real-media validation is not required. Python impact: changes settings-patch orchestration and network-facade integration with focused facade, Local API, network, and WebView regression coverage. Immutable audit evidence remains read-only.
